context.title: The Second Census
context.summary: After the plague, a new count of fighting men totals 601,730; the land is to be divided by tribe size and by lot, and none of the first census remain except Caleb and Joshua.
context.background: Nearly forty years have passed since chapter 1, and a whole generation has died in the wilderness (vv. 64–65). Some tribes grew while others shrank; Simeon fell most sharply, from 59,300 to 22,200 (1:23; 26:14).

customs.note: Casting lots was a way of leaving a decision to God. Larger tribes received more land, but the location was decided by lot.

watchFor: The daughters of Zelophehad are named (v. 33), setting up chapter 27.
The census confirms God's word in 14:29–30 (vv. 64–65).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4).

people.name: Pallu
people.summary: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9.

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

people.name: Carmi
people.summary: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

people.name: Korah
people.summary: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution.

people.name: Abiram
people.summary: One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron.

people.name: Dathan
people.summary: Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

people.name: Nemuel
people.summary: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

people.name: Jamin
people.summary: The Jaminite clan.

people.name: Jemuel
people.summary: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: Son of Simeon.

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18).

people.name: Ozni
people.summary: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Er
people.summary: Birth.

people.name: Onan
people.summary: Strong, the second son of Judah (Gen. 38:4-10; comp. Deut. 25:5; Matt. 22:24).

people.name: Pharez
people.summary: Pharez,, breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

people.name: Shelah
people.summary: Judah’s third son (Gen. 38:2, 5, 11, 14).

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

people.name: Hamul
people.summary: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Tola
people.summary: Eldest son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Puah
people.summary: The sons of Issachar.

people.name: Jashub
people.summary: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Shimron
people.summary: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Elon
people.summary: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

people.name: Sered
people.summary: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Machir
people.summary: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29).

people.name: Gilead
people.summary: Son of Manasseh.

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2).

people.name: Helek
people.summary: A portion, (Josh. 17:2), descended from Manasseh.

people.name: Shechem
people.summary: A descendant of Manasseh (Num. 26:31; Josh. 17:2).

people.name: Hepher
people.summary: The youngest son of Gilead (Num. 26:32; 27:1).

people.name: Zelophehad
people.summary: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness. Having left no sons, his daughters, concerned lest their father’s name should be “done away from among his family,” made an appeal to Moses, who, by divine direction, appointed it as “a statute of judgment” in Israel that daughters should inherit their father’s portion when no sons were left (Num. 27:1-11).

people.name: Tirzah
people.summary: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

people.name: Hoglah
people.summary: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

people.name: Mahlah
people.summary: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

people.name: Milcah
people.summary: Belonged to clans of Menasseh.

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Son of Ephraim.

people.name: Tahan
people.summary: Of the Tahanite clan.

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Bela
people.summary: The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38; “Belah,” Gen. 46:21).

people.name: Huram
people.summary: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

people.name: Naaman
people.summary: Head of Naamites.

people.name: Ard
people.summary: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar.

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Hushim
people.summary: Son of Dan.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

people.name: Imnah
people.summary: The first-born of Asher.

people.name: Heber
people.summary: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

people.name: Serah
people.summary: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Guni
people.summary: Son of Naphtali.

people.name: Jahzeel
people.summary: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Merari
people.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Kohath
people.summary: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11).

people.name: Gershon
people.summary: Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Amram
people.summary: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses (Ex. 6:18, 20; Num. 3:19).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20).

people.name: Jochebed
people.summary: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59).

people.name: Ithamar
people.summary: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4).

people.name: Abihu
people.summary: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office (Ex. 28:1).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1).

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: Sinai
places.summary: Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus.
